turns.q: Can I buy the battery packs from Brightcell Energy? They quote £104.
turns.reply:
No, you cannot buy battery packs from Brightcell Energy. 

Orders may only be placed with active suppliers in the supplier master (POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 6.1), and Brightcell Energy is not yet onboarded (2026-10-19 Weekly purchasing meeting). Furthermore, battery packs are lithium-cell parts, requiring an approved UN 38.3 test report on file before ordering (POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 6.2). Under AMD-SUP-2026-02 (§ 1.1), that report must have been issued within the last 12 months and be valid for at least 60 days past the order date; Brightcell's report is currently being renewed and is not expected until December 2026 (2026-10-22 Quotation Q-BE-26-0917). Finally, a cheaper quote on its own does not justify switching suppliers for a lithium-cell part when a current rate contract exists with Voltway (POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 6.4; 2026-10-23 RE: Brightcell quote).

turns.q: What does ERR-PO-0412 mean and how do I fix it?
turns.reply:
ERR-PO-0412 means "TAX CODE DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER COUNTRY" (MAN-PUR-72 v7.2.3, p.10, § 17.2). It occurs because Fetch automatically defaults the tax code to VAT20-UK, but the supplier is based overseas (shown by the country letters in brackets at the end of the message) (QRC-03 v2026.1, p.1).

To fix it:
1. Check the country letters shown in brackets on the error message (QRC-03 v2026.1, p.1).
2. If the supplier is outside the UK, change the tax code from VAT20-UK to VAT20-RC (or VAT5-RC for reduced-rate goods) (QRC-03 v2026.1, p.1).
3. Keep the cursor in the line details area and press F8 to save again (QRC-03 v2026.1, p.1).
